simple.meaning: בֹּר (bôr) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “vegetable lye (from its cleansing ); used as a soap for washing, or a flux for metals.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 2 times across Job, Isaiah, beginning at Job 9:30. Its meaning is built by comparing the passages where Scripture uses it.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בֹּר (H1253).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: בֹּר (bôr) / H1253 is traced through Job 9:30, Isaiah 1:25 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: vegetable lye (from its cleansing ); used as a soap for washing, or a flux for metals
definitions.full: H1253. bor I. בֹּר noun masculine lye, potash , alkali used in smelting metals Isa 1:25 **read probably כַּכֻּר as in a furnace ( 48:10 ); there seems no evidence that 'lye' (i.e. water mixed with the burnt ashes of plants containing potash, used formerly for washing) was ever used in refining gold or silver: compare J. Napier Anc. Workers in Metal {1856}, 15, 20, 25 WAM in Smith DB ii. 368; Amer. Rev. Ed. (1871, vol, iii), 1939 . (see בֹּרִית ).
